title: Buhay Pilipino: news, weather, fiestas, and a little Taglish
objectives: Talk about the news, weather events, traffic and prices
Describe fiestas and community life (bayanihan, barangay, videoke)
Understand what Taglish is and when Filipinos use it
Review and combine the whole B1 toolkit

grammar.title: Talking about the news and the weather
grammar.explanation:
Everyday Filipino small talk runs on three topics: the weather, the traffic, and the prices — usually in that order. The grammar is all yours already; what's new is the framing vocabulary.

Weather events lead the news for good reason: may paparating na bagyo — a typhoon is approaching (note paparating, 'incoming', from dating). Reports use ayon sa + source (Unit 9): Ayon sa ulat, lalakas pa ang ulan mamayang gabi. When storms hit, the phrases everyone listens for: walang pasok — classes/work suspended; suspendido ang klase; may baha sa maraming lugar; nawalan ng kuryente ang buong barangay (your Unit 11 adversative!) and its household name, brownout.

Traffic talk leans on your emotion and mishap grammar: Grabe ang trapiko kanina — the traffic was terrible earlier; naabutan kami ng dalawang oras na trapiko. Prices recycle comparisons and tumaas/bumaba: Tumaas na naman ang presyo ng bilihin — prices of goods went up again.

Hearsay grammar shines here: most news you pass on isn't yours, so daw/raw and ayon sa do constant work: Magpapatuloy daw ang ulan hanggang Linggo. Signal your own doubt with yata, wonder with kaya: Papasok kaya tayo bukas?

examples.tl: Ayon sa balita, may paparating na bagyo sa Biyernes.
examples.en: According to the news, a typhoon is approaching on Friday.

examples.tl: Walang pasok bukas sa lahat ng paaralan — suspendido raw ang klase.
examples.en: No school tomorrow anywhere — classes are reportedly suspended.

examples.tl: Nawalan kami ng kuryente nang tatlong oras kagabi.
examples.en: We lost power for three hours last night.

examples.tl: Grabe raw ang baha sa may palengke; huwag kayong dumaan doon.
examples.en: The flooding near the market is reportedly severe; don't pass through there.

examples.tl: Tumaas na naman ang presyo ng bilihin, kaya nagtitipid kami.
examples.en: Prices of goods went up again, so we're economizing.

grammar.title: Taglish: what it is, and when it's used
grammar.explanation:
Spend a day in Manila and you'll hear sentences like: Na-traffic ako nang sobra, kaya na-late ako sa meeting. I-send mo na lang sa akin ang file, ha? Mag-drive na lang tayo. This is Taglish — fluid mixing of Tagalog and English — and it is not broken language; it's the normal casual register of most urban, educated Filipinos.

The grammar is systematically Tagalog: English roots take Tagalog affixes and behave like any verb. Mag- + drive = mag-drive (nag-drive, nagda-drive, magda-drive); i- + send = i-send (i-i-send... in writing usually i-send pa rin); na- + traffic = na-traffic (got stuck in traffic); magpa-print (have something printed); naka-park (parked). The affix system you spent this level mastering runs the whole show — voice, aspect, causative and all.

When is Taglish used? Casual conversation among city dwellers, office banter, texting, social media, TV hosts. When is it avoided? Formal writing, speeches, news anchoring in Filipino, school Filipino class — and often with elders in the provinces, where deep Tagalog or the local language rules. Using pure formal Tagalog at a Manila merienda can sound stiff; using heavy Taglish in a provincial fiesta speech can sound show-offy (the word for that: maarte).

As a learner: understand Taglish always, produce it lightly, and keep building the Tagalog core — the affixes are what make even English words behave.

examples.tl: Na-traffic ako sa EDSA nang dalawang oras.
examples.en: I was stuck in traffic on EDSA for two hours.

examples.tl: I-send mo sa akin ang mga litrato pag-uwi mo.
examples.en: Send me the photos when you get home.

examples.tl: Nagpa-print ako ng mga dokumento sa computer shop.
examples.en: I had documents printed at the computer shop.

examples.tl: Mag-drive na lang tayo para hindi tayo mag-antay ng bus.
examples.en: Let's just drive so we don't wait for a bus.

examples.tl: Sa speech contest, huwag kang mag-Taglish — puro Filipino dapat.
examples.en: In the speech contest, don't use Taglish — it should be pure Filipino.

grammar.title: The B1 toolkit in one story
grammar.explanation:
Everything in this level is one machine. Watch it run in a single stretch of talk about fiesta week:

Bago ang pista, nagpalinis kami ng buong bahay at nagpaluto ng lechon (causative, Unit 3). Sabi ng kapitan, magsisimula raw ang parada nang alas-otso (reported speech, Unit 9). Pagdating ng banda, biglang bumuhos ang ulan (pag- clause and pacing, Unit 11); nabasa tuloy ang mga banderitas (accidental na- and tuloy, Units 2 and 5). Kung nakinig sana kami sa balita, nagdala sana kami ng mga tolda (unreal conditional, Unit 7). Buti na lang, tumulong ang buong barangay — bayanihan kung tawagin — kaya natuloy pa rin ang handaang inihanda ng aming mga nanay (relative clause, Unit 8). Nakakapagod, pero sa tingin ko, ito ang pinakamasayang pista na napuntahan ko (nakaka- adjective, opinion frame, and abilitative, Units 4, 6, 2).

If you can follow that paragraph — and better, retell it — you are operating at B1. The exam ahead certifies exactly this: choosing the right focus, stacking the right particles, reporting, wishing, narrating. Balikan mo ang mga nakaraang aralin kung may kulang ka pa; kapag handa ka na, sagutin mo ang pagsusulit. Kaya mo ito.

examples.tl: Ipinagawa ng barangay ang entablado bago ang pista.
examples.en: The barangay had the stage built before the fiesta.

examples.tl: Sabi ng lola ko, mas masaya raw ang pista noong araw.
examples.en: My grandma says fiestas were merrier in the old days.

examples.tl: Kung hindi umulan, natuloy sana ang parada sa plaza.
examples.en: If it hadn't rained, the parade would have pushed through at the plaza.

examples.tl: Ang pinakahihintay ng lahat ay ang videoke sa gabi.
examples.en: What everyone waits for most is the videoke at night.

examples.tl: Sa tingin ko, ang bayanihan ang pinakamagandang ugali ng mga Pilipino.
examples.en: In my view, bayanihan is the finest trait of Filipinos.

vocab.note: Kumusta ang panahon? = how's the weather?; noong panahon ni Lola = in Grandma's time

example.tl: Masama raw ang panahon bukas, kaya mag-ingat kayo sa biyahe.
example.en: The weather will reportedly be bad tomorrow, so be careful traveling.

example.tl: Pinalakas ng bagyo ang hangin at ulan buong gabi.
example.en: The typhoon strengthened the wind and rain all night.

vocab.note: bumabaha = it floods; binaha ang kalye = the street got flooded

example.tl: Hanggang tuhod ang baha sa amin kagabi.
example.en: The flood at our place was knee-deep last night.

example.tl: Lumabas kami agad ng gusali nang lumindol.
example.en: We immediately left the building when the earthquake hit.

example.tl: Bumalik na ang kuryente pagkatapos ng tatlong oras.
example.en: The electricity came back after three hours.

vocab.note: the standard Filipino term for a blackout

example.tl: Tuwing may bagyo, inaasahan na namin ang brownout.
example.en: Whenever there's a typhoon, we already expect a power outage.

example.tl: Walang pasok bukas dahil sa paparating na bagyo.
example.en: No classes/work tomorrow because of the approaching typhoon.

example.tl: Suspendido ang klase sa lahat ng antas ngayong araw.
example.en: Classes at all levels are suspended today.

vocab.note: casual: trapik; Taglish: na-traffic ako = I got stuck in traffic

example.tl: Grabe ang trapiko papuntang Quezon City tuwing Biyernes.
example.en: The traffic going to Quezon City is terrible every Friday.

vocab.note: also spelled piyesta; pista ng bayan = town fiesta

example.tl: Uuwi kami sa probinsya para sa pista ng bayan.
example.en: We're going home to the province for the town fiesta.

example.tl: Dumaan ang parada sa harap mismo ng bahay namin.
example.en: The parade passed right in front of our house.

example.tl: Hanggang hatinggabi ang videoke ng mga kapitbahay namin.
example.en: Our neighbors' videoke went on until midnight.

vocab.note: from bayan; neighbors banding together to help

example.tl: Sa bayanihan, sama-samang inayos ng mga kapitbahay ang nasirang bubong.
example.en: In the spirit of bayanihan, the neighbors fixed the damaged roof together.

example.tl: Nagpadala ang barangay ng tulong sa mga naapektuhan ng baha.
example.en: The barangay sent help to those affected by the flood.

vocab.note: nine dawn masses from Dec 16; bibingka and puto bumbong outside the church

example.tl: Kumpleto raw ang hiling mo kapag natapos mo ang siyam na Simbang Gabi.
example.en: They say your wish comes true if you complete the nine dawn masses.

example.tl: Maaga pa lang, pinag-uusapan na ang susunod na eleksyon.
example.en: Even this early, the next election is already being talked about.

example.tl: Ayon sa gobyerno, aayusin daw ang mga kalsada bago ang Pasko.
example.en: According to the government, the roads will supposedly be fixed before Christmas.

vocab.en: prices of goods, cost of living

example.tl: Laging usapan sa palengke ang presyo ng bilihin.
example.en: Prices of goods are always the talk of the market.

example.tl: Tumaas ang presyo ng gasolina nang dalawang piso.
example.en: The price of gas went up by two pesos.

example.tl: Magpapatuloy daw ang ulan hanggang Linggo.
example.en: The rain will reportedly continue until Sunday.

vocab.en: to text, send a text message
vocab.note: Taglish, fully standard: nag-text, nagte-text, magte-text

example.tl: Mag-text ka sa akin pagdating mo sa bahay.
example.en: Text me when you get home.

vocab.note: Taglish i- pattern with English roots: i-send, i-download, i-print

example.tl: I-send mo sa akin ang litrato ng parada mamaya.
example.en: Send me the photo of the parade later.

vocab.note: iulat = to report; ulat-panahon = weather report

example.tl: Ayon sa pinakabagong ulat, ligtas na ang lahat ng pasahero.
example.en: According to the latest report, all the passengers are safe.

example.tl: Naglinis ang mga estudyante ng kapaligiran pagkatapos ng pista.
example.en: The students cleaned up the surroundings after the fiesta.

example.tl: Handa ang barangay namin sa anumang kalamidad.
example.en: Our barangay is prepared for any calamity.

vocab.note: from maghanda; paghahanda sa bagyo = storm preparations

example.tl: Isang linggo ang paghahanda namin para sa pista.
example.en: Our preparations for the fiesta took a week.

example.tl: Huwag kang masyadong maarte sa pagkain kapag bisita ka.
example.en: Don't be too fussy about food when you're a guest.

dialogue.title: Bago ang pista, may bagyo
dialogue.context: Neighbors Aling Cely and Marco talk over the fence about the typhoon news and the coming fiesta.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Aling Cely, narinig ninyo po ba ang balita? May paparating daw na bagyo sa Biyernes.
lines.en: Aling Cely, did you hear the news? A typhoon is reportedly coming on Friday.

lines.speaker: Aling Cely
lines.tl: Naku, oo. Ayon sa ulat kaninang umaga, malakas daw ito. Paano na ang pista sa Sabado?
lines.en: Oh yes. According to this morning's report, it's supposedly strong. What about the fiesta on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Sabi po ng kapitan, ipagpapaliban daw ang parada kung hindi hihina ang ulan.
lines.en: The captain said the parade will be postponed if the rain doesn't weaken.

lines.speaker: Aling Cely
lines.tl: Sayang naman ang mga banderitas na inilagay natin. Sana naman huwag masira.
lines.en: Such a waste of the banners we put up. I do hope they don't get ruined.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Nag-text na po ako sa mga pinsan ko sa Maynila. Baka raw hindi sila makabiyahe.
lines.en: I already texted my cousins in Manila. They said they might not be able to travel.

lines.speaker: Aling Cely
lines.tl: Kung ako sa kanila, aalis na ako bukas ng umaga bago lumakas ang hangin.
lines.en: If I were them, I'd leave tomorrow morning before the wind picks up.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Tama po kayo. O, kumpleto na po ba ang paghahanda ninyo? Baka magbrownout na naman.
lines.en: You're right. And are your preparations complete? There might be another power outage.

lines.speaker: Aling Cely
lines.tl: Handa na: may kandila, de-lata, at tubig. Noong isang taon kasi, nawalan kami ng kuryente nang dalawang araw.
lines.en: All set: candles, canned goods, and water. Last year, you see, we lost power for two days.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Kami rin po. Buti na lang, nagtulungan ang buong barangay noon.
lines.en: Us too. Luckily, the whole barangay helped one another back then.

lines.speaker: Aling Cely
lines.tl: Iyan ang maganda sa atin — bayanihan kapag may kalamidad.
lines.en: That's what's beautiful about us — bayanihan when there's a calamity.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.tl: Opo. At kapag lumipas na ang bagyo, ituloy natin ang pista. May videoke pa rin po ba?
lines.en: Yes. And once the typhoon passes, let's push through with the fiesta. Will there still be videoke?

lines.speaker: Aling Cely
lines.tl: Aba, siyempre! Walang pistang matatapos nang walang kantahan, ulan man o araw.
lines.en: Well, of course! No fiesta ever ends without singing, rain or shine.

reading.title: Ang pistang inabot ng bagyo
reading.tl:
Tuwing ikatlong linggo ng Mayo ang pista ng aming bayan, at isang buwan ang paghahanda: nagpapagawa ng entablado ang barangay, nagpapaluto ang bawat pamilya, at nagsasabit kami ng mga banderitas sa buong kalye.

Noong isang taon, dalawang araw bago ang pista, nagbago ang ulat-panahon: may paparating daw na bagyo. Nag-alala ang lahat. Kinagabihan, lumakas nga ang hangin, nagbrownout, at binaha ang plaza. Kung hindi sana naglipat ng mga upuan at tolda ang mga kabataan bago lumakas ang ulan, nasira sana ang lahat.

Pagkalipas ng bagyo, hindi pa rin sumuko ang bayan. Sa diwa ng bayanihan, naglinis ang lahat ng kapaligiran: may nagwalis, may nag-ayos ng entablado, may nagluto para sa mga naglilinis. Naitapos ang lahat sa loob ng isang araw. Natuloy ang pista, mas masaya pa yata kaysa dati. Sabi nga ng lola ko habang kumakanta sa videoke: ang ulan, lumilipas; ang pista, hindi.
reading.en:
Our town fiesta falls on the third week of May, and the preparation takes a month: the barangay has a stage built, every family has food cooked, and we hang little banners along the whole street.

Last year, two days before the fiesta, the weather report changed: a typhoon was said to be approaching. Everyone worried. That night, the wind did strengthen, the power went out, and the plaza flooded. If the young people hadn't moved the chairs and tents before the rain intensified, everything would have been ruined.

After the typhoon passed, the town still didn't give up. In the spirit of bayanihan, everyone cleaned the surroundings: some swept, some fixed the stage, some cooked for those cleaning. Everything was finished within one day. The fiesta pushed through, even merrier than before, it seemed. As my grandmother said while singing at the videoke: the rain passes; the fiesta doesn't.

choices: There's no food tomorrow
No work or classes tomorrow
Nobody is entering tomorrow
The door is closed tomorrow
exercises.explain: Walang pasok is the fixed announcement that work/classes are suspended — what everyone listens for when a typhoon nears.

exercises.prompt: In 'Na-traffic ako kaya na-late ako sa meeting', what makes this Taglish still grammatically Tagalog?
choices: The English words are unchanged
English roots carry Tagalog affixes and aspect (na-traffic, na-late)
The word order is English
It uses no particles
exercises.explain: Taglish runs on Tagalog grammar: English roots slot into the affix system (na-, mag-, i-, magpa-) with normal aspect marking.

exercises.prompt: ___ sa ulat, lalakas pa ang ulan mamayang gabi. (According to the report...)
exercises.explain: Ayon sa + source attributes information: ayon sa ulat, ayon sa balita, ayon kay Lola.

exercises.prompt: Nawalan kami ng ___ nang tatlong oras dahil sa bagyo. (We lost electricity for three hours...)
exercises.explain: Nawalan ng kuryente — the Unit 11 adversative applied to the most typhoon-typical loss: power.

exercises.prompt: Where would heavy Taglish be LEAST appropriate?
choices: Texting a Manila officemate
Chatting at a mall food court
Delivering a formal Filipino speech at a school program
Joking with city friends at a videoke night
exercises.explain: Formal speeches, Filipino class, and news anchoring call for pure Filipino; Taglish lives in casual urban registers.

exercises.tl: Suspendido raw ang klase bukas dahil sa bagyo, pero may pasok pa rin daw ang mga opisina.
choices: Classes and offices are both suspended tomorrow
Classes are reportedly suspended tomorrow, but offices still have work
Offices are suspended but classes continue
Everything is closed because of the flood
exercises.explain: Suspendido ang klase = classes suspended; pero may pasok pa rin ang mga opisina = offices still open. Raw/daw marks both as relayed news.

exercises.prompt: Prices of goods went up again, so we are economizing.
exercises.answer: Tumaas na naman ang presyo ng bilihin, kaya nagtitipid kami.
accept: Tumaas na naman ang presyo ng bilihin kaya nagtitipid kami
Tumaas na naman ang presyo ng mga bilihin, kaya nagtitipid kami
Tumaas ulit ang presyo ng bilihin kaya nagtitipid kami
exercises.explain: Na naman = 'again (annoyingly)'; kaya links to the consequence; magtipid (Unit 7) in the incompleted aspect for the ongoing habit.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW (Unit 1): 'I'll cook the kaldereta for the fiesta' — the kaldereta is definite. Which is right?
choices: Magluluto ako ng kaldereta para sa pista.
Lulutuin ko ang kaldereta para sa pista.
Niluto ko ang kaldereta para sa pista.
Magluto ka ng kaldereta para sa pista.
exercises.explain: A definite object takes object focus, contemplated aspect: lulutuin ko ang kaldereta. Choice 1 makes it indefinite; choice 3 is past.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW (Unit 3): ___ ng barangay ang entablado bago ang pista. (The barangay had the stage built — thing in focus, completed)
exercises.explain: Having something built with the thing in focus is ipagawa; completed: ipinagawa ng barangay ang entablado.

exercises.prompt: Kung hindi sana naglipat ng mga tolda ang mga kabataan, nasira sana ang lahat.
exercises.answer: If the young people hadn't moved the tents, everything would have been ruined.
accept: If the young people hadn't moved the tents, everything would have been ruined
If the youth had not moved the tents, everything would have been destroyed
Had the young people not moved the tents, everything would have been ruined
exercises.explain: Unreal past conditional (Unit 7): kung + completed + sana in both clauses — the moving happened, so the ruin didn't.

exercises.tl: Pagkalipas ng bagyo, naglinis agad ang buong barangay, at natuloy pa rin ang pista kinabukasan.
choices: The fiesta was canceled for the year
The whole barangay cleaned up right away and the fiesta still pushed through the next day
Only the plaza was cleaned a week later
The barangay postponed the cleanup until after the fiesta
exercises.explain: Pagkalipas ng bagyo = after the typhoon passed; naglinis agad = cleaned right away; natuloy pa rin = still pushed through.

exercises.prompt: Send me the photos of the parade later, okay? (casual, Taglish i- verb)
exercises.answer: I-send mo sa akin ang mga litrato ng parada mamaya, ha?
accept: I-send mo sa akin ang mga litrato ng parada mamaya, ha
I-send mo sa akin mamaya ang mga litrato ng parada
I-send mo sa akin ang mga picture ng parada mamaya ha
Ipadala mo sa akin ang mga litrato ng parada mamaya
exercises.explain: Taglish i-send follows the i- focus pattern exactly — the definite photos are the ang-phrase; pure-Tagalog ipadala works too.
